plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
The remaining portfolio focuses on income and broad market exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month, but actual returns are not guaranteed. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to reduce overall leverage and meet the combined limit.
Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name concentration rule.
Buy OXY at 4% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a diversified approach.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by reducing overall leverage and diversifying slightly. It aims for risk-first growth, blending broad index exposure with quality tech and a small allocation to leveraged ETFs. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with potential for steady growth.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
Add to all existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to 6% each, pressing into working assets.
Buy OXY at 6% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan aggressively uses leverage and concentrates in high-scoring setups for stretched growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and concentration, but actual returns are not guaranteed. It significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lose a lot fast; strict stop discipline is critical. Expect higher volatility and larger potential drawdowns.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero to prioritize low drawdown.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on rotating into income-generating assets.
The goal is steady monthly distributions with reduced growth focus.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by prioritizing steady monthly distributions, but actual returns are not guaranteed. It cuts leverage and high-beta names to near zero, focusing on income and broad index ETFs. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account. Expect lower growth potential but a focus on consistent cash flow.
